text:
There are a few things we can enhance. First, make the input device detection automatic rather than fixed. In the settings, there should be an option to change the microphone, but on the onboarding page, it should auto-detect and also provide an option to add or change the input device directly. Currently, the input device is fixed, so users cannot change it or add an option there to auto-detect their specific device. Additionally, add a horizontal bar to show volume detection, making it noticeable that the volume is being detected while speaking. Replace the green light circular blinking effect with audio waveforms on the green dots, but do not remove the existing effect; just add the waveform effect. Apply the same changes to the onboarding page.

Next, remove the three dots, specifically the red, yellow, and green indicators, and do not do anything else with that section for now. We can talk about that later. Also, remove the GitHub and docs links from the about page. While private and local features are present, they are not the main feature, so we cannot market it as such. However, it is fine to leave that information at the bottom for version 1, so do not change that. Finally, make the hotkey customizable, as it is currently not customizable.

It's not like it's a typeable thing, so I don't think that's good. Make that fix and we are good to go. When they press it, they should have an option to choose their key combination. So whenever they press the keyboard, they can choose the combination, and escape cancels it, leading to the default, which is control space. Right. As for audio, like advanced, remove all those. I think okay, let it be; that's fine, we can check. All right, history works fine, everything works fine, so the basic app is ready. So change all this, we are good to go then.

Also, add guidance so people can understand which model to choose, like in the Groq cloud search provider. Have an option that names the models so we can understand which is faster, which is better, and what each one does. This is really important because normally people would choose larger models like Large V3, and it takes more time to transcribe, making them think the app is slow. So let them know by having transcription settings separately in the sidebar. When they click, they can see the models and cleanup mode in detail, explaining what they actually do, rather than having it buried in the general settings. That's one thing you can do, and we are good to go. I can't change the UI at all; the existing design is fine. Everything should be preserved, including the design. This is version one, which is ready. Let's do it, and we are good to go.

I really like the work that has been done in Astra, so I want to merge it with master. I want to keep everything from the Astra branch because it is end-to-end and everything works properly in that commit. For anything that conflicts or is different in master, remove that and keep the Astra version. We are good to commit this now. Do a merge commit with a message like "Production ready UI version 1" or "Finalized UI." Merge Astra with the master branch, and if there are any conflicts, resolve them by removing the master code. I want everything in my master branch to be as good as it is in the Astra branch.
